title: Historic Fire Hall No. 1 adaptive reuse concepts in City technical feasibility report
code_edition: National Building Code – 2019 Alberta Edition (cited in the 2022 study for accessibility; the governing edition for a future application is not established)

facts.text: The City EOI identifies Historic Fire Hall #1 at 140 6 Avenue SE, Calgary, built in 1911, two storeys, City-owned and a legally protected heritage asset; potential uses included food/beverage, theatre, rehearsal, meeting and event space.

The 2022 feasibility report states its accessibility review uses NBC 2019 Alberta Edition; it reports no passenger elevator at the time, recommends one, calls for a barrier-free main entrance, and says washrooms, stairs and floor changes need review.

The report presents food/beverage (Group A, Division 2; assumed 225 people) and theatre (Group A, Division 1; assumed 175–200 people) concepts. Both list no existing fire separation and show a proposed new stair/elevator; the hose tower is marked heritage-sensitive. These are concept assumptions, not approved plans.

The report says occupant loads are code-based calculations whose accuracy depends on the future operator’s internal layout; furniture is shown only for rough load estimates; proposed architectural changes require feasibility assessment and barrier-free access must be revisited.

The attached main-floor plan sheet A202 is marked “Issue for Report” dated 2021-05-28 and says it must not be used for construction until approved; it also notes interior construction as per A.B.C.-2019(AE).

limitations: This is a documented City feasibility study, not an applicant submission or variance decision.
The 2021 architectural set is explicitly “Issue for Report,” not approved for construction.
The City master plan and EOI are shared sources with the separate North-West Travellers candidate; the cases represent distinct building-specific slices, not separate application files.
No AHJ determination for a future permit is included.
